content.title: About
content.content: Barley bread is made from whole barley grain or flour, often blended with wheat. It has a dense crumb, a mildly nutty flavor, and a dark‑golden crust. Barley is rich in fiber and β‑glucan, making this bread nutritious and filling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Barley is one of the oldest cultivated grains, grown by humans for over 10,000 years.
In ancient Egypt barley bread was offered to the gods as a sacred food.
The high β‑glucan content can help lower cholesterol levels.
Barley contains antioxidants such as selenium and vitamin E.
Traditional Scandinavian “rugbrød” often combines barley and rye flours.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar.

items.title: Contains β‑glucan
items.content: This soluble fiber can reduce LDL cholesterol and support immune function.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Barley provides thiamine, niacin, and folate, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: It supplies magnesium, phosphorus, iron, and zinc, which aid muscle and nerve health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Compared with white wheat bread, barley bread raises blood glucose more slowly.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Barley contains gluten, so the product is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High phytic acid
items.content: Phytic acid can impair mineral absorption; soaking or fermenting the dough can reduce its level.

items.title: Cereal allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to barley.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Barley bread works well toasted, in sandwiches, as a soup side, or as a base for breadcrumbs. It can be grilled with olive oil and herbs or used for open‑face toppings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the bread in a paper bag or bread box at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze it in an airtight bag for up to 2 months. Thaw at room temperature before use.

content.title: About
content.content: Cereal, cinnamon toast is a dry whole‑grain wheat flake coated with aromatic cinnamon and sugar. It is designed for a quick breakfast: just add milk or yogurt and wait a few minutes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first ready‑to‑eat flakes appeared in the United States in the early 20th century as a convenient way to consume grain.
The cinnamon used in this product is rich in antioxidants and gives it a warm, distinctive aroma.
The formula often includes whole grains, increasing fiber content compared with regular sweet cereals.
The product is marketed as a “5‑minute breakfast” and is popular among busy consumers.
Packaging is usually made from recyclable plastic, reducing its environmental footprint.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Whole‑grain flakes provide sustained energy and help maintain satiety.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and contributes to normal cholesterol levels.

items.title: Contains cinnamon antioxidants
items.content: Cinnamon has anti‑inflammatory properties and may aid glucose metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The product contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Fortified with B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and B6 help support the nervous system and energy metabolism.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweetened cereals can contain a notable amount of sugar, which is undesirable for people with diabetes or those trying to lose weight.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Made from wheat, the product is not suitable for individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Possible additives
items.content: Some versions may contain artificial flavors and preservatives that could trigger reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Overconsumption
items.content: Large portions can lead to excess calorie and sugar intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Place a serving of flakes in a bowl, pour milk, yogurt, or a plant‑based drink over them, stir and wait 2–3 minutes. You can add fresh fruit, nuts, or honey for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cereal in its original package or an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. When stored properly, it remains fresh for up to 12 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Organic ready-to-feed infant formula is designed for babies from birth to 12 months. It is made from certified organic ingredients, contains no GMOs, artificial preservatives, or flavors. The formula provides a balanced ratio of proteins, fats, carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals essential for infant growth and development.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The formula is produced from whole organic cow's milk that is pasteurized at low temperature to preserve nutrients.
All ingredients are certified according to USDA Organic standards (or equivalent in the country of manufacture).
Ready-to-feed format is packaged in sterile single-use containers, eliminating the need for sterilization before feeding.
The formula includes prebiotics that support the development of a healthy gut microbiome in infants.
The product has undergone clinical trials confirming its safety and efficacy.

items.title: Supports growth and development
items.content: A balanced mix of proteins, fats, and carbohydrates provides energy and building blocks for tissue growth.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2, B6, and B12 support nervous system development and metabolism.

items.title: Immune system support
items.content: Vitamin A, vitamin D, and zinc help strengthen the infant's immune defenses.

items.title: Bone health
items.content: Calcium and phosphorus together with vitamin D promote strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Digestive health
items.content: Prebiotics and a modest amount of dietary fiber aid normal digestion and help prevent constipation.

items.title: Cow's milk protein allergy
items.content: Some infants may develop an allergy to cow's milk protein; discontinue use and consult a pediatrician if symptoms appear.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: While no added sugars are present, natural lactose is included; infants with lactose intolerance require special attention.

items.title: Shelf life after opening
items.content: Once opened, the formula should be used within 24 hours and kept refrigerated to prevent bacterial growth.

items.title: Not suitable after 12 months
items.content: After one year, nutritional needs change, and age‑appropriate foods should be introduced.

content.title: How to Feed
content.content: Shake the container before use, open the single‑use spout, and dispense the ready product into a clean bottle. Do not heat in a microwave; warm the bottle in warm water to about 37 °C. If dilution is required, follow the manufacturer’s instructions.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened containers in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and use within 24 hours. Discard the product if it develops an off‑smell, color, or taste.

orange-juice-100-canned-bottled-or-in-a-.title: Orange juice, 100%, canned, bottled or in a carton

content.title: About
content.content: 100 % orange juice is a completely natural beverage made from fresh oranges without added sugar, preservatives, or flavorings. It is available in canned jars, glass bottles, and carton packs, providing convenient storage and transport.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oranges used for juice are rich in vitamin C, one of the most powerful antioxidants.
Proper pasteurization and airtight packaging can retain up to 90 % of the vitamins.
In some countries, orange juice is traditionally served fresh‑pressed, but industrial juice retains much of the flavor thanks to rapid processing.
Carton packs are made from recyclable materials and often feature an aluminum foil layer to protect against light.
Canned juice is frequently used in cooking for marinades, sauces, and desserts.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system, aids collagen synthesis, and improves iron absorption.

items.title: Contains flavonoids
items.content: Flavonoids such as hesperidin have antioxidant effects and may support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: One cup (250 ml) of orange juice contains about 110 kcal, making it a light snack option.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal blood pressure.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Natural acids and dietary fiber in the juice aid digestion and can help relieve constipation.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although 100 % juice contains no added sugar, natural sugars can raise the glycemic index, which is important for people with diabetes.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity may irritate the stomach lining in individuals with gastritis or reflux.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to oranges.

items.title: Vitamin loss over time
items.content: Vitamin C can degrade during prolonged storage after opening, so consume the juice soon after opening.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the juice chilled, use it in smoothies, cocktails, marinades, sauces, and desserts. When adding to hot dishes, incorporate the juice at the end of cooking to preserve flavor and nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened packages in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep in the refrigerator for 3–5 days, sealing tightly or transferring to an airtight container.

content.title: About
content.content: Hard plain salted pretzels are a baked snack made from wheat flour, water, yeast and salt, shaped into the iconic twisted knot and baked until crisp. They have a mildly salty, slightly sweet flavor and a crunchy texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pretzels have ancient origins, with ancestors dating back to medieval Europe.
They are traditionally associated with Bavarian beer culture and are often served with beer.
The knot shape symbolized crossed arms, a medieval German sign of blessing.
Hard salted pretzels are usually sprinkled with coarse sea salt, enhancing their taste.
In the 19th century United States, pretzels became a popular street snack.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Hard pretzels provide a quick source of energy thanks to their high complex carbohydrate content.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many snack foods, they contain virtually no fat, making them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: The wheat flour used supplies modest amounts of iron, which supports blood formation.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 aids protein metabolism and supports the nervous system.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The added salt helps maintain electrolyte balance, though intake should be monitored.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: The amount of salt can raise blood pressure in salt‑sensitive individuals.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Pretzels contain wheat, so they are unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While low in fat, the carbohydrate content makes them fairly calorie‑dense if eaten in large portions.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to wheat flour.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pretzels are convenient as a standalone snack, paired with cheese, mustard, hummus, or added to salads. A quick warm‑up in the oven restores extra crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent moisture absorption and loss of crispness.
